identity.name: Later Liang
alt_names: Later Liang of the Sixteen Kingdoms

land.text: Liang province and the Hexi corridor, seized by Lü Guang in 386

predecessors.note: Cliopatria has Former Liang (324-377) before; Former Qin conquered it in 376.

successors.note: Cliopatria draws it as Later Qin only from 407.

capitals.name: Guzang (Wuwei)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Guzang, modern Wuwei, Gansu.

rulers.name: Lü Guang
rulers.note: Duke of Jiuquan 387 (page text); King of Sanhe 389; Heavenly King of Great Liang 396.

rulers.name: Lü Long
rulers.note: Infobox gives 403; the text has the throne passed to him in 401.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 387 shape (Hexi to Dunhuang) taken back one year

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "Historians consider this the beginning of the Later Liang dynasty" in 386 (infobox "Established: 386", capital Guzang) while Cliopatria starts in 387. The 387 shape is carried back one year.

237,231 km2 for 387-396: the Hexi corridor from Wuwei to Dunhuang with a stretch of Ningxia; the page says only that the state "controlled the Hexi Corridor at its peak" and gives no infobox area, so no figure comparison was possible. Lü Guang conquered Kucha in 384 as a Former Qin general; the shape does not reach the Tarim. Outline beyond the places named is unverified: page budget.

86,136 km2 for 397-401: "Southern Liang and Northern Liang broke away, leaving Later Liang's territory reduced to its capital region in central Gansu". The Northern Liang 397 shape lies inside the 387 shape (471 of its 472 cells), consistent with the page. Ningxia cells (28) in the shape are unexplained. Outline beyond the places named is unverified: page budget.

84,602 km2 for 402-406, but the page ends the state in 403: "Lü Long surrendered the entire territory to Later Qin and moved to Chang'an, ending the Later Liang." The shape holds only 402-403; Cliopatria's Later Qin shape does not take Wuwei until 407 (Later Qin dossier carries the 403 gain).

region.text: Guzang, where Lü Guang introduced a new reign era in 386

ledger.note: 386: Lü Guang founds Later Liang at Guzang. "Historians consider this the beginning of the Later Liang dynasty," after Lü Guang introduced a new reign era at Guzang; infobox "Established: 386". Lü Guang had been sent to the Western Regions in 383 and "conquered Kucha" in 384.

region.text: Liang province: Guzang and the Hexi corridor

ledger.note: 386: Lü Guang seizes Liang province. "In 386, Lü Guang, returning from the Western Regions, seized Liang province" (Former Qin page), founding Later Liang.

region.text: Longxi, where the Western Qin fought Later Liang

ledger.note: 391: Later Liang begins its war with Western Qin. "He fought Western Qin in Longxi" in 391-395 (page gives the span); the Western Qin page: "After conflict from 391 onward" the Qifu moved their capital to Xicheng.

region.text: Western Qin: Longxi and the upper Yellow River

ledger.note: 395: Western Qin submits briefly. He fought Western Qin "forcing them into submission briefly in 395" (Later Liang page); the Western Qin page has the Qifu "briefly submitted to Later Liang (after 395)".
395: the Longxi war ends in a short submission of the Qifu.

region.text: Western Qin: Longxi and the upper Yellow River

ledger.note: 397: Lü Guang's campaign against Western Qin fails and the submission lapses. "Lü Guang's campaign against Western Qin failed"; the page does not date the end of the submission, so 397 is the failed campaign's year.

region.text: the Northern Liang breakaway: the Zhangye, Jiuquan and Dunhuang oases of Hexi

ledger.note: 397: Northern Liang breaks away. "Southern Liang and Northern Liang broke away, leaving Later Liang's territory reduced to its capital region in central Gansu." Lü Guang had claimed the title Heavenly King of Great Liang in 396.

region.text: the Southern Liang breakaway round Lanzhou and the upper Yellow River

ledger.note: 397: Southern Liang breaks away (same sentence). The region is the researcher's reading of Cliopatria's Southern Liang 397 shape.

401: Later Qin besieges Guzang. Later Qin "forced the Later Liang into submission after besieging their capital" in 401; the Later Liang page: Lü Long submitted as a vassal with the title Duke of Jiankang, "401-403 (no exact year given)", while Southern and Northern Liang continued attacking him.
403: Lü Long surrenders the whole territory. "Lü Long surrendered the entire territory to Later Qin and moved to Chang'an, ending the Later Liang."
403: the siege and vassalage end in surrender.

region.text: the Later Liang realm at its end

ledger.note: 403: the Later Liang ends. Infobox "Disestablished: 403"; successor states listed on the page: Southern Liang, Northern Liang, Later Qin. Lü Long was executed in 416 after Yao Bi's failed coup.

wars.name: Later Liang-Western Qin war
wars.outcome: Western Qin forced into brief submission in 395; Lü Guang's 397 campaign failed.

wars.name: Secession of Northern Liang and Southern Liang
wars.outcome: Both broke away in 397, leaving Later Liang its capital region.
wars.note: The page does not describe fighting.

wars.name: Later Qin subjugation of Later Liang
wars.outcome: Guzang besieged, Lü Long a vassal (Duke of Jiankang), the whole territory surrendered in 403.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: Hexi oases, the Western Qin frontier and the Later Qin frontier are named by city and region, not by line.

notes: Cliopatria's Later Liang row 387..406 starts a year late (386) and runs three years past the state's end in 403 (the Later Qin took the whole territory then; Cliopatria gives Wuwei to Later Qin only in 407). Wikidata: Cliopatria's 'Later Liang Dynasty' (911-925, Q783489 shared with Liang Dynasty) is a different, Five Dynasties state; this dossier is the Sixteen Kingdoms Later Liang and does not touch it. The Later Liang page gives no infobox area, so no figure comparison was made (Cliopatria maximum 237,231 km2). Budget 1-2 pages: Later Liang, plus the Former Qin and Later Qin pages opened for siblings. Not settled: the Western Liang (founded 400 at Dunhuang, Cliopatria 407-409) is not on the Later Liang page; the Western Regions (Kucha, Shanshan, Gaochang) are not on the page either; the date of the Later Qin siege (401-403 span); the date the Western Qin submission ended. Counterparts: northern-liang, southern-liang, western-qin, later-qin, former-qin all have dossiers or will.
